content: I'm building a CLI tool in Rust to dedupe large files by content hash. Sketch the architecture — modules, data flow, and the key crates you'd reach for. Keep it concrete.
Good. Now write the core dedupe function with a streaming hasher (blake3) so it handles 100 GB files without loading them into memory. Show the full function.
Walk through the memory profile of that function — where the allocations are and whether it could OOM on a 32 GB machine under heavy concurrency.
Add parallelism with rayon, but cap concurrency so we don't thrash the disk with too many simultaneous reads. Show the updated code.
Switch gears: explain the difference between content-defined chunking (FastCDC) and fixed-size chunking for dedup ratio, and when each wins.
Write me a short haiku about deduplication to lighten the mood.
Back to the code — what was the FIRST function I asked you to write earlier in this conversation? Refactor it to return a Result<_, std::io::Error> instead of panicking on a read failure.
Summarize everything we've built across this whole session and the key design decisions we made along the way.
